items.title: Accusing wife of adultery for speaking to male friend is cruelty: Jharkhand High Court
items.summary: The Jharkhand High Court recently observed that accusing one's wife of adultery for merely speaking to her male friend amounts to mental cruelty. A Bench of Chief Justice MS Sonak and Justice Manoj Prasad made the observation while dismissing a man’s plea seeking divorce from his wife. One of the allegations made by the husband was that his wife was in an extra-marital relationship as she used to talk to an unknown male over mobile phone. “To our considered view, such allegations are typical gender-based stereotypes, where, if a woman talks to a man, even if he is a friend, charges of adultery or of an extramarital relationship are levelled. We are, therefore, of the considered view that such allegations amount to cruelty towards the wife,” the Court said. Chief Justice MS Sonak, Justice Manoj Prasad The couple had married in 2005 and have two children. In 2021, the husband moved a family court seeking dissolution of marriage, alleging that his wife was not interested in the marital relationship. He claimed there were frequent quarrels between them as she used to continuously talk to a male friend over the phone. It was also stated that she had left the matrimonial home in 2015 and gone to her parental home. However, the wife alleged that she was tortured at her matrimonial home over dowry. She also said that her husband never tried to restore conjugal life or make any effort to bring her back to her matrimonial home. The trial court ruled in favour of the wife in 2023, ruling that the allegations of cruelty were not made out. The husband then moved the High Court. In a judgment passed on November 3, the High Court agreed with the finding that the husband had failed to prove his allegations of cruelty against wife. The witnesses produced by him were outsiders to the marriage, it noted. “Two of them appear to be his colleagues and friends, who are not family members. Their evidence, therefore, cannot be accepted without an element of suspicion. items.title: Calcutta High Court dismisses NGO's plea for enquiry into demolition of its book stall during Durga Puja
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court on Tuesday dismissed Association for Protection of Democratic Rights' (APDR's) plea seeking an impartial, time-bound enquiry into identifying and holding accountable the persons responsible for the demolition of their temporary book stall near Jadavpur 8B Bus Stand without any prior notice during Durga Puja [Association for Protection of Democratic Rights v. The State of West Bengal and Ors.]. Justice Rishad Medora dismissed the plea on the ground that since the book stall was erected without the appropriate permission, no fundamental right of the petitioner (ADPR) was infringed. However, he noted that that ADPR was free to opt for any other remedy it deemed appropriate in pursuit of its enquiry into the demolition of its stall. "It does not appear that any fundamental right of the petitioner has been violated for it to approach this Court in its writ jurisdiction. Since no affidavit has been called for, the allegations made in the writ petition are deemed not to have been admitted by the respondents. The petitioner will be at liberty to pursue other remedies, if any, available to it in respect of the aforesaid demolition. The writ petition stands dismissed with the aforesaid observations and directions," the Court said. According to the plea, the dispute arose when people claiming to be from the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) accompanied by a sizeable police contingent allegedly forcibly ransacked and demolished ADPR's temporary book stall in the middle of Durga Puja festivities. ADPR said that this step came after it had made representations to the Joint Commissioner of Police as well as the Assistant Director, Borough X, KMC seeking necessary permissions to erect and operate its book stall. The requisite municipal fee was also deposited with the KMC. No communication to the contrary was received from any of these authorities after receiving ADPR's application seeking permission, the plea said. The petitioner further added that subsequent representations detailing this incident to the Home Minister of the State, Municipal Commissioner and the Inspector General of Police and Vigilance Authority fell on deaf ears. items.title: Possibility of crime no ground to restrict operating hours of licensed bars: Kerala High Court
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Tuesday held that the Police cannot impose restrictions on the timings of DJ parties conducted by establishments with appropriate liquor licences (FL-3 permits) that allow their operation during extended hours [ Mahadevan v State of Kerala & ors ]. Justice Murali Purushothaman opined that the mere possibility of criminal activities is no ground to impose restrictions on the operation of such facilities. " The mere possibility of criminal activities cannot, by itself, constitute sufficient justification for imposing restrictions under the Kerala Police Act on the extended operating hours of the FL-3 hotel permitted under the Foreign Liquor (Amendment) Rules, 2026" the Court said. The Court held that while the Police have a responsibility to curb crime, it cannot restrict the activities of licenced bars by merely citing suspicions of criminal activities like drug use at such premises, unless rules restricting such bar timings are put in place by the State. "If the police have reason to believe that criminal activities are taking place under the guise of DJ parties in hotels, it is the responsibility of the police to take stringent action in accordance with law to curb the same...Until the government frames appropriate rules prescribing exception to the extended hours of operation permitted in the Foreign Liquor Rules, the police cannot curtail or restrict the operating hours of the hotel contrary to the provisions granted under those Rules in the absence of special grounds justifying such restrictions, " the Court held. items.title: Telangana orders statewide probe into illegal human egg harvesting racket
items.summary: Telangana Health Minister C Damodar Rajanarasimha has ordered a detailed investigation into the alleged illegal harvesting and commercial sale of human eggs in the state, following the arrest of eight people in Hyderabad on October 30. Police also rescued 43 women during the operation. The Minister instructed health officials to identify those involved and initiate strict action against institutions and individuals violating the law. Subsequently, task force teams stepped up inspections of in-vitro fertilisation (IVF) centres across Telangana. Authorities have inspected 27 of the 44 registered assisted reproductive technology (ART) facilities in the state. The inspections revealed 13 violations across seven hospitals, prompting officials to issue show-cause notices to the managements. Checks at the remaining facilities are continuing. The health department is also examining documents seized by the police and seeking information from the National Assisted Reproductive Technology and Surrogacy Registry. A team of state officials visited the registry's office in New Delhi on November 6 to obtain details submitted by registered clinics and banks operating in Telangana. Investigators are examining the involvement of doctors, fertility centres, intermediaries, and women identified in the case. Police have stated that the accused brought women from West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, and other states to Hyderabad, where they were accommodated and recruited for egg extraction procedures. The health department reiterated that all human egg harvesting procedures must comply with the Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Act and its rules. It also cautioned women against financial inducements and misleading promises from intermediaries, urging them to report suspicious activities to their district medical and health officers. items.title: Karnataka Muslim group flags alleged disproportionate deletion of Muslim voters during SIR
items.summary: The Karnataka Rajya Muslim Okkoota (KRMO) has questioned the deletion of voters during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. It has sought an explanation from the Election Commission of India (ECI), citing data that shows Muslims were disproportionately represented in certain deletion categories. In a statement on Monday, November 9, the organisation said an analysis of booth-level data published by the ECI, conducted by political research consultancy Sankalp, found that 27.59% of voters had been deleted across the 10 Assembly constituencies represented by Muslim MLAs. This was higher than the statewide deletion rate of 19.45%. The 10 constituencies had 9,62,359 Muslim voters on the 2025 electoral rolls. Of these, 2,46,759, or 25.64%, were deleted during the revision. The overall deletion rate in these constituencies was 27.59%, while the rate among voters from other communities was 28.79%. The analysis also found that more than 8.80 lakh Muslim voters were deleted across 64 constituencies where Muslims account for at least 15% of the electorate. Of the 38,82,598 Muslim voters on the 2025 rolls in these constituencies, 8,80,543, or 22.67%, were removed. The deletion rate among other voters in these constituencies was 20.19%. KRMO also pointed to the distribution of deletion categories across Karnataka. Of the 15,15,088 voters deleted under the 'absent' category, 2,58,770 were Muslims. Similarly, Muslims accounted for 1,43,940 of the 7,08,666 voters removed under the 'already enrolled elsewhere' category. According to the analysis, Muslims accounted for 12.9% of voters on the state's 2025 electoral rolls, but made up 17.1% of those deleted as absent and 20.3% of those removed as already enrolled elsewhere. By contrast, 2,00,277 Muslim voters were deleted under the 'dead' category, accounting for 12.2% of all voters removed on that ground. The organisation argued that the difference was significant because deaths can be verified against official records. At the same time, classifications such as absent or already enrolled elsewhere depend substantially on assessments made by Booth Level Officers (BLOs) and other field officials. items.title: Cybercriminals siphon Rs 22.3 cr from Tamil Nadu rural healthcare funds
items.summary: Cybercriminals allegedly siphoned off Rs 22.30 crore from a bank account maintained by Tamil Nadu’s Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department. The money, allocated for rural healthcare infrastructure, was transferred through 46 unauthorised transactions using the department’s online banking system. The fraud came to light after KR Ramprasad, a Block Development Officer and Superintendent attached to the Directorate of Rural Development and Panchayat Raj, lodged a complaint with the Chennai Police Commissioner. According to the complaint, Rs 22,30,04,879 was transferred from the department’s Single Nodal Account with HDFC Bank’s CIT Nagar branch between October 12 and 30. The account, held in the name of the Director of Rural Development and Panchayat Raj, contained funds released by the Union and Tamil Nadu governments under the Fifteenth Finance Commission’s Health Sector Grants. The grants, covering the period from 2021-22 to 2025-26, are intended to strengthen primary healthcare infrastructure and services in rural areas through Rural Local Bodies. The department had authorised Block Development Officers of Block Panchayats to operate the account and make payments to contractors through an online portal. Each officer was provided an individual user ID and password, and transactions required authorisation through a maker-checker system. No other person was authorised to initiate or approve payments. The complaint alleges that unidentified persons gained unauthorised access to the account and transferred the money without the knowledge or approval of the department. Preliminary verification of bank statements and transaction records revealed 46 electronic debits that had not been initiated or approved by any authorised official. The transactions were reportedly routed through maker and checker accounts mapped to Block Development Offices in Keezhaiyur in Nagapattinam district, Mandapam in Ramanathapuram district and Dharapuram in Tiruppur district. items.title: HC directs Tamil Nadu govt to file district-wise report on SC/ST Act implementation
items.summary: The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court has directed the Tamil Nadu government and the Director General of Police (DGP) to file a comprehensive, district-wise statistical report on the implementation of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act in the last five years. The report is to be submitted to the court on November 24. The court was hearing a plea filed by Kathir, the founder-director of the Madurai-based rights organisation, Evidence. Most notably, the High Court has demanded details of the total number of cases registered under the Act and the number of cases in which investigation has been completed in each district. Other significant vectors the court has ordered include the number of cases in which charge sheets have been filed; the number of cases in which charge sheets are yet to be filed; the number of cases pending trial before the respective courts; the number of cases disposed of during the relevant period; and the number of cases resulting in acquittal and conviction, respectively. The court has also ordered the state government and police to provide details of the number of cases in which the opinion of the Director of Prosecution was sought for filing an appeal or seeking enhancement of sentence. Further, details of the number of cases in which appeals have been filed before the Madras High Court and the Supreme Court against an acquittal are also to be provided. “In the past eleven years [2015–2025], approximately 3,800 cases registered under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act have resulted in acquittals. However, it is reported that the state government has filed appeals in only 13 of these cases,” a press statement from Kathir said. Evidence also pointed to a significant gap between the number of acquittals and the number of appeals filed by the state government, despite the Act’s provision to file appeals. “In this regard, I filed a public interest litigation (PIL) seeking appropriate directions to ensure that the state government takes necessary action to file appeals against acquittal in accordance with the provisions of the Act,” Kathir added. Referring to the court’s order, Kathir also said, “This is an important development in our collective efforts to strengthen the implementation of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and ensure justice for survivors.”
